```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```

```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```

```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they’re already the correct next steps given there are no PASS candidates and nothing inconclusive.

## 1) Select best module candidate (AUB autopilot)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for:
- It should run the candidate sweep defined by `module_registry.yaml`, score them, and (with `--select-best`) promote the best-performing candidate into the “current” slot used by subsequent steps.
- Confirm it prints the chosen candidate and where it wrote updated artifacts (often a “latest” or “selected” JSON).

## 2) Run system-level candidates
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to look for:
- This tests end-to-end/system configurations (not just module-level tweaks).
- Capture the resulting report path and any “best” summary table.

## 3) Generate the next recommended fix
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What to look for:
- `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` should contain the next actionable change suggestion based on the latest runs (and it’s useful for creating the next candidate set).

## Quick sanity checks if something looks off
- Ensure `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` is readable and is the baseline the tools expect.
- If step (1) doesn’t “select” anything, it usually means no candidates improved the objective or the registry has no eligible candidates.

If you paste the stdout from command (1) and (2) (or the generated report links/paths), I can tell you whether the selection and system runs look healthy and what the next fix is pointing at.
